clue.text: America wants first place to get an advantage

indicators.note: the clue says America wants the place to come first, so that piece leads the answer

parts.note: Pl. is the standard abbreviation for place in street addresses
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: The United States insists on finishing top to gain an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a point in someone's favour, a benefit or asset.

clue.text: Gee — Old Glory ill befits a British PM!

indicators.note: ill befits suggests the letters are a poor fit as they stand and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Goodness, the American flag hardly suits a British prime minister!
explanation.walkthrough: Old Glory is a nickname for the US flag.
explanation.definitionFit: David Lloyd George was Liberal Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1916 to 1922.

clue.text: A Catholic turning up among various saints as church officer

indicators.note: among places the other letters inside the mixed ones
various indicates the letters of saints are mixed
in a down clue turning up means read from the bottom, so these letters go backwards

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A Catholic rises among a group of saints to take a role in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' flips only the Catholic abbreviation, giving CR after the A; 'various' jumbles saints into SISTAN, which takes ACR after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristan is the official in charge of a church's sacristy and its sacred vessels.

clue.text: Crazy Spooner's scattered rubbish

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words are exchanged by sound

parts.note: scattered means strewn, said 'stroon'
muck is filth or rubbish

explanation.surface: A mad person's rubbish lies scattered about, as Spooner might say.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of STREWN MUCK ('stroon muck') gives 'moon struck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being moonstruck was once thought to be caused by the moon, so it means mentally deranged or crazed.

clue.text: Husband's warlike temper initially lowering a bit

indicators.note: lowering a bit means moving the letter slightly further down in this down entry

parts.note: martial means warlike

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of temper

explanation.surface: A husband's fiery temper starts to cool a little.
explanation.walkthrough: In MARTIAL the T moves one place down to give MARITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital originally meant relating to a husband, from the Latin maritus.

clue.text: Friend of Dr Johnson holds tome — Virgil, in translation

indicators.note: in translation implies the words are rendered into another form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar's companion owns a volume of Virgil in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' looks like a container signal but is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish writer of The Vicar of Wakefield was a member of Samuel Johnson's literary Club.

clue.text: Sort of mist that's a worry in Dover?

parts.note: Dover is a port town on the sea, facing the Channel
to fret is to worry; a fret is a state of worry

explanation.surface: Coastal fog is a concern for the cross-Channel port of Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the loose link: a worry at a seaside town like Dover is a fret at the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a cold wet mist rolling in from the sea onto England's east coast.

clue.text: Acceptable language from superior wise man

parts.note: U means upper-class or socially superior in British ...
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A guru speaks proper English.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the customary way words are used, the accepted norms of a language.

clue.text: Anchor Jack finally put over side

indicators.note: in a down entry put over means placed above the next piece
finally picks the last letter of Jack

parts.note: an edge is a side

explanation.surface: A sailor finally lowers the anchor over the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A kedge is a small anchor used to warp a ship along.

clue.text: One may get squeezed at a musical gig

definitions.text: One may get squeezed at a musical gig

parts.words: One may get squeezed at a musical gig
parts.note: reads like a fan crushed in the crowd at a show, but describes a small bellows instrument that is played by squeezing

explanation.surface: A fan risks getting crushed in the crowd at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: This small hexagonal accordion makes its sound when the player squeezes its bellows together.

clue.text: Novelist unhappy about Chopin's end?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for unhappy wraps around the other letter

parts.note: unhappy means sad

indicators.note: end picks out the last letter of Chopin

explanation.surface: A writer grieves over the death of the composer Chopin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: George Sand, the French novelist, was Chopin's lover for nearly a decade.
explanation.definitionFit: George Sand was the pen name of the nineteenth-century French writer Aurore Dupin.

clue.text: Daughter in a quarrel getting nowhere?

indicators.note: in tells us the daughter's letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a rift is a breach between people, a quarrel
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A girl caught up in a family row feels her life is going nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is adrift floats aimlessly without direction, making no progress toward a destination.

clue.text: One should sit close to the organ for audibility

definitions.text: One should sit close to the organ for audibility

parts.words: One should sit close to the organ for audibility
parts.note: suggests a churchgoer sitting near the organ to hear it, but the organ is the ear and the thing sits in or against it to make sound audible

explanation.surface: Advice to a hard-of-hearing churchgoer to sit by the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A headphone or receiver unit is held against the ear so the listener can hear.

clue.text: Those who know congestion can be bad supporting an end to traffic

indicators.note: an end to picks the last letter of traffic
can be bad suggests the letters go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Experts say traffic jams can be awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of CONGESTION plus C, the last of traffic, give the answer; 'supporting' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The cognoscenti are connoisseurs, people with expert knowledge of a subject.

clue.text: Group's entertaining number charged with emotion?

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of holding a guest, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people; the run of letters across Group's entertaining is a coincidence, not the setter's device
N is the usual algebraic symbol for a number

explanation.surface: A band plays an emotionally charged song.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent in slang means thrilled or carried away, filled with ecstatic feeling.

clue.text: Job of a bargeman in a less serious era

parts.note: lighter means less serious, more frivolous
an age is an era

explanation.surface: Working a barge was a job of a more carefree time.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighterage is the business of transferring cargo by flat-bottomed barge, called a lighter, between ship and shore.

clue.text: Buttress for church needing restraint on top

indicators.note: on top means placed above the other pieces in this down entry

parts.note: a rein is a restraint
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church wall needs bracing at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttress something is to support or strengthen it.

clue.text: Flowering plant not in good shape in Spanish city

indicators.note: in places the word for unwell inside the city's name

parts.note: Granada is a city in Andalusia, southern Spain
ill means unwell, not in good shape

explanation.surface: A plant is wilting in the heat of a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a passionflower species, the climbing vine that bears passion fruit.

clue.text: Sound of stroke by man at wicket, funny-looking character

parts.note: a ding is a ringing sound of a blow
the batsman at the wicket in cricket is the bat

explanation.surface: A cricketer hits the ball with a clunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A dingbat is a typographic ornament or symbol, an odd-looking printed character.

clue.text: Broken heart absorbing negative reply in a second

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the reply goes inside
broken means the letters of heart are mixed

parts.note: no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: A broken-hearted lover hears a refusal in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges the letters into ATHER, with the reply going in just after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means one more, an additional or second one.

clue.text: Dramatic technique cut short in the golf club

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: dramatic irony is a device where the audience knows more than the characters

explanation.surface: A theatrical device is used sparingly at the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a type of golf club with a metal head, used for shorter shots.

clue.text: Matches terribly dead when lacking ace among the players

indicators.note: among puts the jumbled letters inside the word for players

parts.note: wings are players on the flanks in rugby or hockey

indicators.note: terribly signals that the remaining letters are jumbled
when lacking says a letter is removed from the word dead

parts.note: A is short for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A team plays dreadfully when its star is missing from the line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when lacking' leaves DED and 'terribly' turns it into EDD. Wings are flank players in rugby or hockey, which is what makes 'the players' fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a marriage, so weddings are matches in the sense of unions.

clue.text: Twig decaying — no indication of wood growth

indicators.note: no means without, so these letters are removed

parts.note: withering means decaying
a tree's annual ring shows a year's wood growth

explanation.surface: A twig is rotting with no sign of new growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A withe is a flexible twig such as willow, used for binding.

clue.text: Poet's basic assumption

definitions.meaning: a given, the premise from which a story or argument starts, borrowed from French

explanation.surface: A poet's fundamental premise.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was the metaphysical poet; donne (or donnée) is a given starting assumption.

clue.text: Skating no longer a professional business?

parts.note: off means no longer on, finished
skating takes place on ice

explanation.surface: Someone hangs up their skates to take a desk job.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Skating no longer' as being off the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional such as a solicitor runs their practice from premises known by this name.

clue.text: Kingdom banishing a secret society

indicators.note: banishing means sending away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Tonga is a Pacific island kingdom

explanation.surface: A monarchy drives out an underground organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tong is a Chinese secret society or criminal association, especially in American Chinatowns.

clue.text: Gay circle talking foolishly

parts.note: gay in its older sense means carefree, blithe
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A cheerful group chatters away nonsensically.
explanation.definitionFit: To blither is to babble or prattle senselessly, so this present participle means chattering nonsense.

clue.text: Attractive person who grabs a pupil?

definitions.meaning: someone striking who draws everyone's gaze
a playful reading: one who seizes the pupil, the dark centre of the eye

explanation.surface: A good-looking teacher has a way of capturing a student's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone noticeably striking draws looks; literally the phrase is one who seizes the eye's gaze.

clue.text: Old-fashioned poetry about this ruler

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: rime is an archaic spelling of rhyme, verse

explanation.surface: Antique verse written about a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler, prince or commander, as in the Gulf states.
